Gated docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-024.md (branch feature/WF02-REQ-024, commit 41df5f7) independently. Read core-directives.md, WF-02 Step 3b, docs/agents/design/REQ-024.md in full (AC1-AC5, AC-empty/schema/deps/catalog, and the design's own SS0-SS6), then the real implementation (apps/bot/src/domain/qr.ts, apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts's getMyRegistrations/getWaitlistPosition/withdrawRegistration/promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible, apps/bot/src/handlers/my.ts), then the test spec file itself end to end -- not TEST-DESIGNER's own claims about it.

Coverage check: every AC (AC1-AC5) plus AC-empty, AC-schema, AC-deps, AC-catalog has at least one verification case with an exact command, exact fixture SQL/TS, exact expected value, and an explicit Pass/FAIL condition. Grepped the spec for 'TODO' -- zero hits. No case relies on subjective judgment: every expected value is a literal string/count/SQL predicate (e.g. exactly 3 sends, position text 'Your position: 2'->'Your position: 1', a literal grep pattern with an exact expected match count).

AC2 auto-promotion trigger verified directly against source (task step 3): apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts lines 537-561 -- withdrawRegistration captures `wasAdmitted = row.admission === 'admitted'` BEFORE the UPDATE (line 540), then calls `promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible(tx, row.eventId, at)` (line 559-561) if and only if wasAdmitted is true, in the SAME transaction. The spec's capacity-1 fixture (SEATHOLDER admitted, AHEAD waitlisted position 1, VIEWER waitlisted position 2) withdraws SEATHOLDER -- an admitted row -- which structurally satisfies wasAdmitted and genuinely invokes promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible (lines 361-421+), which locks the events row, re-counts admitted seats fresh, and promotes the earliest-created waitlisted candidate (AHEAD, by created_at asc per its own candidate-selection query at lines 409-415) to admitted. This is a real, different code path from BACKEND-DEV's own AC2 case (a capacity-0 event where nothing is ever admitted, so wasAdmitted is always false and promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible is never reached at all). getWaitlistPosition (lines 266-296+) re-queries live state on every call (no caching, confirmed by reading its body: two fresh SELECTs against current admission/created_at state) so VIEWER's recomputed position (AHEAD now admitted, no longer counted as 'ahead-and-waitlisted') correctly drops from 2 to 1 purely as a byproduct of AHEAD's promotion, never a write to VIEWER's own row -- getMyRegistrations (lines 617-637) is a plain SELECT with no UPDATE anywhere in its body, and withdrawRegistration's own UPDATE (line 543) targets only the withdrawn row's id, never VIEWER's. The spec's byte-identical updated_at check (toISOString string equality) is therefore a sound test of this claim. Trigger construction is CORRECT.

AC3 loop-capture-bug-catching capability verified directly against source (task step 4): apps/bot/src/handlers/my.ts line 76, `for (const row of rows) { ... }` -- a for-of loop with `const row`, which creates a fresh, independently-scoped binding per iteration in JS/TS (not `var`, which would be reused/mutated across iterations and could produce the classic closure-capture bug). Per this codebase's CURRENT implementation, the classic shared-variable-reference bug is not structurally reachable via the loop variable itself. However, the spec's AC3 case does not merely grep for `var` vs `const` -- it exercises actual runtime behavior: two admitted registrations for the same user, two distinct real tokens (obtained via registerForEvent, confirmed non-equal), and asserts each of the two decoded photo contents matches ITS OWN row's token specifically (not just 'some valid QR was sent twice'). This is a behavioral case, not merely structural, so it would also catch a DIFFERENT bug with the same symptom that IS live-reachable in the current code: `renderCheckInQrPng` (apps/bot/src/domain/qr.ts) takes `qrToken` as a plain input parameter with no memoization/module-level cache in its current implementation (confirmed by reading its 12-line body: composes the string, calls `QRCode.toBuffer` fresh, no caching) -- but if a future change introduced any per-call caching keyed incorrectly, or reintroduced a shared mutable variable anywhere in the per-row loop body (e.g. hoisting `qrToken` or the composed deep-link string outside the loop by mistake during a refactor), this two-distinct-token case is the only one in this codebase that could catch it; BACKEND-DEV's own single-admitted-row AC3 case structurally cannot, since there is only one token to compare against itself. Capability is CORRECTLY CONSTRUCTED and honestly scoped (the spec's own failure-mode text names a hypothetical loop-capture bug as one instance of a broader wrong-token-per-row class, not a claim that the bug exists today).

Cross-checked exact expected values against the real implementation (task step 5): catalog.my.header ('Your registrations:'), catalog.my.emptyState ('You have no registrations yet. Check /events to find one.'), catalog.my.withdrawButton ('Withdraw') all confirmed verbatim at apps/bot/src/i18n/en.ts lines 200-202; catalog.registration.waitlistedPositionPrefix ('Your position:') confirmed at line 168; STATUS_CATALOG_KEY confirmed exported at apps/bot/src/handlers/registration.ts line 21; the 'requested' AdmissionState enum value confirmed at apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts line 179 (pgEnum 'admission'); apps/bot/package.json confirmed qrcode 1.5.4 under dependencies (line 16) and jsqr 1.4.0/pngjs 7.0.0/@types/pngjs 6.0.5/@types/qrcode 1.5.6 all under devDependencies (lines 21-24), exactly as AC-deps claims; i18n parity (header/emptyState/withdrawButton) confirmed present in types.ts (lines 236-238) and ru.ts (lines 207-209) in addition to en.ts, matching AC-catalog's claim.

No mocked/stubbed grammY Context anywhere (task step 6): the spec's Shared Setup section (step 7) explicitly reuses REQ-020's established harness shape (real Bot instance, bot.handleUpdate, captured sendMessage/sendPhoto array against api.config.use) verbatim, and AC3's decode path is confirmed to use the real jsqr/pngjs devDependencies (grepped apps/bot/src/domain/qr.test.ts's own header comment, which the spec explicitly says to copy verbatim for the .default-vs-callable interop) -- no stub decoder or mocked grammY Context appears anywhere in the spec's own cases or its reused existing-test pointers.

Failure-mode statement check (task step 7): every AC section (AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC-empty, AC-schema, AC-deps, AC-catalog) ends with explicit 'Pass conditions' and a named FAIL/'Failure mode this catches' describing the exact regression it exists to detect. None left implicit. The coverage table cross-references every AC against its verification with an explicit 'Would fail if violated?' column, all answered Yes with a concrete violation description.

Spot-checked the Independence note's claims about BACKEND-DEV's existing coverage against the actual test files (not taken on faith): grepped apps/bot/src/handlers/my.test.ts's describe/it labels -- 'REQ-024 AC1' (line 239), 'REQ-024 AC2' (line 321), 'REQ-024 AC3/AC4/AC5' (line 389) all present and match the spec's cited line numbers/descriptions; apps/bot/src/domain/qr.test.ts's two cases (lines 42-55, 57-63) also match.

No check failure found. PASS.
